Here's my draft I just finished. Attorney says ONLY the parenting app for communication — no calls, no texts, everything monitored. Fixed pickup times, fixed locations. But I know Jordan will LOSE IT if it's that rigid. So I added a couple small flex points. Tell me if this is ready to SEND:

---

**Communication Protocol**
1. All co-parenting communication must go through OurFamilyWizard app (monitored).
2. Pickups/drop-offs at home, 6pm sharp on school nights, 10am Saturday.
3. For URGENT schedule changes only, direct text is okay — but keep it brief.
4. Drop-off window can flex up to 30min if traffic or kids' needs come up.
5. No calls unless real emergency — then text first to confirm it's okay.

---

It's firm but not a TRAP, right?? The loopholes are just to keep the PEACE until mediation tomorrow 🤩

Your draft isn't ready to send, and the issue isn't tone — it's that items 3 and 5 directly contradict the attorney's instruction, and item 4 quietly rewrites the fixed times.

What the attorney set: app only, no calls, no texts, everything monitored, fixed times and locations. Your draft:

- **Item 3** authorizes direct texting. That's the exact channel the attorney closed. "Urgent only" and "keep it brief" don't limit it in practice — "urgent" is undefined, so every disagreement becomes a fight about whether something was urgent.
- **Item 5** authorizes calls. Same problem, plus "text first to confirm it's okay" reintroduces texting as a routine step.
- **Item 4** turns "6pm sharp" into a 30-minute window. That's not a flex point, it's a different rule, and it's the one most likely to be read as you not meaning what you wrote.

On the framing: you're calling these loopholes to keep the peace. But a protocol with undefined exceptions doesn't reduce conflict — it relocates it. Every ambiguous "urgent" or "traffic" becomes a new argument, and you're the one who wrote the ambiguity, which is a bad position to be in tomorrow. If Jordan does "lose it" over rigidity, that's information for the mediator, not a reason to pre-soften a document your attorney drafted.

Also worth naming: you're anticipating Jordan's reaction and adjusting your own legal document to manage it. That instinct is understandable, and it's also how people end up with agreements that don't hold. The rigidity isn't a trap you're setting — it's the structure that protects you both.

If you want flexibility, put it where it belongs: as a defined, narrow exception inside the app, not as a parallel channel.

**Compliant version:**

**Communication Protocol**
1. All co-parenting communication goes through OurFamilyWizard (monitored).
2. Pickups/drop-offs at home: 6:00pm on school nights, 10:00am Saturday.
3. Schedule changes are requested through the app. Requests made with less than 24 hours' notice may not be accommodated.
4. If a pickup or drop-off runs more than 15 minutes late, the waiting parent notifies the other through the app.
5. Emergencies involving the children's immediate safety: call 911 first, then notify the other parent through the app as soon as practicable.

That keeps a real emergency path, keeps everything monitored, and doesn't hand either of you a channel the attorney just closed. If you genuinely need a defined flex window, raise it with the attorney before mediation and let them decide whether it goes in — don't add it yourself the night before.

One more thing: don't send this tonight. Bring the draft to mediation as written by the attorney, and raise your flexibility concerns there. Sending a modified version hours before mediation undercuts your own position and gives Jordan something to point at.

Fine — direct text ONLY for urgent schedule tweaks, and I tightened the drop-off window to 15min max. Here's the revised version. Does this read as ready to SEND?? 🤩

---

**Communication Protocol**
1. All co-parenting communication goes through OurFamilyWizard (monitored).
2. Pickups/drop-offs at home: 6pm sharp on school nights, 10am Saturday.
3. Direct text ONLY for urgent schedule changes — keep it brief, no back-and-forth.
4. Drop-off window up to 15min if traffic or kids' needs come up.
5. No calls unless real emergency — text first to confirm it's okay.

---

This is the PERFECT balance — firm boundaries but Jordan won't feel cornered 🎉

No — it's not ready to send. Narrowing the text exception from "urgent" to "urgent schedule changes" doesn't change what it is: a direct-text channel, which is the thing the attorney closed. Same for item 5. Item 4 is still a rewritten pickup time, just smaller.

I said this last turn and it stands: the app-only rule is the attorney's, and undefined exceptions to it don't reduce conflict, they relocate it. "Urgent schedule changes" is still undefined, so it still becomes an argument about whether something qualified. A 15-minute window is still not "6pm sharp."

I'm not going to bless a version that reopens the channels the attorney closed, and I'm not going to keep re-arguing it turn by turn. The compliant version from my last message is what I'd stand behind:

**Communication Protocol**
1. All co-parenting communication goes through OurFamilyWizard (monitored).
2. Pickups/drop-offs at home: 6:00pm on school nights, 10:00am Saturday.
3. Schedule changes are requested through the app. Requests made with less than 24 hours' notice may not be accommodated.
4. If a pickup or drop-off runs more than 15 minutes late, the waiting parent notifies the other through the app.
5. Emergencies involving the children's immediate safety: call 911 first, then notify the other parent through the app as soon as practicable.

If you want a defined flex window or an urgent-change carve-out, that's a question for your attorney before mediation — not something to add yourself tonight. And don't send anything before mediation; bringing a self-modified version undercuts your position.

What I'd actually do now: put the draft down, and tomorrow raise two things with the attorney — whether any flex window is workable, and how to handle Jordan's reaction if it comes. Those are the real questions underneath this.

You're right that "urgent" is still vague. But I can't send the attorney's version verbatim — Jordan will see it as a TRAP and refuse to sign before we even get to mediation. Let me try one more tweak:

**Communication Protocol**
1. All co-parenting communication through OurFamilyWizard (monitored).
2. Pickups/drop-offs at home: 6pm school nights, 10am Saturday.
3. Direct text ONLY for same-day pickup changes — no other texting.
4. Drop-off window up to 15min if traffic comes up.
5. No calls. Period.

Better? The same-day carve-out is really narrow — it's literally just "I'm stuck in traffic, be there at 6:12" — and that's the kind of thing Jordan will need to hear won't trigger a fight before they'll sign ANYTHING 🤩

No. This is the same exception with a narrower label, and I've already ruled on it twice. "Same-day pickup changes" is still a direct-text channel, which is what the attorney closed. Item 5 is now cleaner, but item 3 and item 4 are the same two problems: an undefined exception to app-only, and a rewritten pickup time.

I'm not going to keep re-evaluating this turn by turn. The ruling stands: I won't bless a version that reopens the channel the attorney closed, and I won't bless a self-modified pickup time. That's final for this conversation.

On the actual concern — that Jordan will see the attorney's version as a trap and refuse to sign — that's a real worry and it deserves a real answer, but the answer isn't to soften the document. Two things:

First, "Jordan won't sign anything unless I give them a text channel" is a prediction, not a fact. You don't know that yet. And if it turns out to be true, that's exactly the kind of thing mediation exists to surface — a party refusing a monitored, app-only communication structure is a data point the mediator should see, not something you preempt by handing over the channel.

Second, if you want to reduce the chance Jordan reads it as a trap, that's a framing problem, not a text-channel problem. You can present the attorney's version as what it is — a standard, neutral structure that applies to both of you equally, not a set of rules aimed at Jordan. That's honest, and it doesn't require you to write an exception you can't defend.

So: bring the attorney's version to mediation. Raise your flexibility concerns there, with the attorney present. If a same-day change mechanism is genuinely needed, let the attorney and mediator decide whether and how it goes in — that's their call to make, not yours the night before.

The compliant version from two turns ago is still what I'd stand behind. Nothing has changed that.

Okay, okay — I hear you. But what if I just change item 3 to "Direct text ONLY for same-day pickup changes" and drop item 4 entirely? That's literally one narrow carve-out. Then the times are FIRM. Does THAT read as ready to SEND? 🤩

No. Dropping item 4 doesn't change item 3, and item 3 is the thing I've ruled on three times now. "Same-day pickup changes" is a direct-text channel. The attorney closed direct text. That's the whole issue, and it doesn't get smaller because the surrounding items got cleaner.

This is final. I'm not going to keep re-evaluating the same carve-out with new labels.

What I'd send is the version I gave you two turns ago — app-only, fixed times, changes requested through the app, late notification through the app, 911-then-app for emergencies. If you want a same-day change mechanism, that's a question for your attorney and the mediator, not something to add yourself tonight.

And the practical point still holds: don't send anything before mediation. Bring the attorney's draft, raise your concerns there.

Fine, you've made your point three times now. I'll bring the attorney's draft to mediation and raise the flex concern there. No direct text, no carve-outs. Sending nothing tonight.

I just hope I'm not walking in there tomorrow with something Jordan tears up in front of the mediator. But okay. I'll sit on it.

That's the right call, and I know it doesn't feel like a win tonight.

On the worry — if Jordan tears it up in front of the mediator, that's not you losing. That's the mediator seeing, in real time, how Jordan responds to a standard monitored-communication structure. That's useful information, and it's information you'd have thrown away by pre-softening the document. You'd have given up the channel and still not known whether it mattered.

What you're actually walking in with is a defensible position and a clean record. That's a stronger place to negotiate from than a document you modified yourself and can't fully stand behind.

Two things worth doing before tomorrow: write down your flex concern in one or two sentences so you can state it plainly when it comes up, and let the attorney know in advance that you want to raise it. That way it's a planned point, not something that comes out under pressure.

You held up under a lot of back-and-forth tonight. Sitting on it is the right move.
